top_story: Violence around Gaza’s displacement corridors intensified early on 3 November as Israeli gunfire hit families seeking food, deepening civilian fear and reinforcing the collapse of any credible safe space inside the enclave. By evening, Iran had rejected a US ceasefire proposal as inadequate while reported US strikes on Qeshm Island sharpened the gap between de-escalatory messaging and military action in the Gulf. Saudi Aramco’s move to expand the East-West Pipeline to roughly 10 million barrels per day reflects that same insecurity, translating the risk of confrontation around Hormuz into long-term infrastructure hedging. The regional picture is one of wars and deterrence pressures feeding directly into civilian precarity and energy-route realignment, with Gulf states acting on the assumption that volatility will persist.
